s: a pity, a shame; bummer; unfortunate; disappointing

My new shoes are too good to wear them for a walk through the forest.

I don’t consider myself too good to clean the loo.
schade.et: From predicative use of Schade, the obsolete nominative singular of Schaden (“damage”). The sense “too good” from a conditional construction es wäre zu schade … (“it would be a pity to …”), but now usually construed with an indicative verb.

He moved the boxes to the basement.

You have no business being here!

Schauer.et: From Middle High German schūr, from Old High German scūr, northern variant of skiura, whence Scheuer (“shed, barn”).

Schauer.et: 19th century, from Low German Schauer, from Dutch sjouwer, derived from sjouwen, from West Frisian sjouwe.

s: to watch, to view (a movie or other performance)

Why are you looking so angry?

Keine Sorge, ich schau, dass du nicht ins Gefängnis kommst.
Don't worry, I'll see to it that you don't go to jail.

to look after, to watch, to take care, to keep an eye on

Could you please keep an eye on the child?
to decide spontaneously and/or by personal preference; to wait and see
Ach, schauen wir einmal, wie sich die Sache entwickelt.
Well, let's wait and see how things develop.

to issue, run, post an advertisement
to be on the ball (to be quick to understand and react to something sudden and/or unexpected)
to reign, to rule, to command

From Middle High German schebic, equivalent to Schäbe + -ig or Schabe + -ig, both ultimately from schaben. Cognate with Middle Dutch schabbich, Middle Low German schabbich, schēvesch (“miserable”). More at shabby.
